questions.prompt: What is a `sealed trait` used for in Scala?

options.text: Restricting all direct subtypes to the *same source file*, enabling the compiler to check `match` exhaustiveness

code.source:
sealed trait Expr
case class Num(n: Int) extends Expr

questions.prompt: What does `Either[Error, Value]` represent, and how is it biased in Scala 2.12+ / 3?

options.text: Models a value (`Right(v)`) OR a typed failure (`Left(err)`); it is *right-biased* so `.map`, `.flatMap`, and `for`-comprehensions operate on `Right`

questions.prompt: Why is `xs.foldLeft(init)(fn)` safer than `xs.reduce(fn)` on an empty collection?

options.text: `reduce` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` on an empty collection; `foldLeft` returns `init`

questions.prompt: What does `case head :: tail => ...` match in a `List` pattern match?

options.text: A non-empty `List`, binding its first element to `head` and the remaining list to `tail`

list match
  case h :: t => h

options.text: The entire matched `Person` instance while also destructuring `age`

questions.prompt: What do `given` and `using` replace in Scala 3 compared to Scala 2 `implicit`?

options.text: `given` defines canonical contextual instances and `using` declares contextual parameters (clarifying intent over overloaded Scala 2 `implicit`)

questions.prompt: What does `extension (s: String) def words: List[String] = ...` (Scala 3) provide?

options.text: Adds `.words` syntax to `String` cleanly without Scala 2 `implicit class` wrapper boilerplate

questions.prompt: What is an `opaque type UserId = Long` in Scala 3?

options.text: A zero-overhead newtype: treated as a distinct `UserId` type outside its defining scope, while compiling to raw unboxed `Long` at runtime

questions.prompt: In Scala variance, what does `trait Producer[+A]` (`+A` covariant) allow?

options.text: Using `Producer[Dog]` wherever `Producer[Animal]` is expected (safe when `A` appears in output/return positions)

questions.prompt: Why is `List[+A]` covariant whereas `Array[T]` (and mutable `ArrayBuffer[T]`) is invariant in Scala?

options.text: Mutable containers cannot be covariant safely (otherwise putting a `Cat` into an `Array[Animal]` alias of `Array[Dog]` would fail at runtime)

questions.prompt: What is a `PartialFunction` vs a total function in Scala?

options.text: A `PartialFunction[A, B]` is defined only for a subset of inputs `A` (checked via `.isDefinedAt`), typically written as `{ case ... => ... }`

questions.prompt: What does `trait A extends B with C` linearization solve in Scala?

options.text: Resolves diamond inheritance deterministically using right-to-left C3-like linearization so `super` calls follow a strict linear chain

questions.prompt: What is a common pitfall of `case class` equality when a field is an `Array[Byte]`?

options.text: `Array` on the JVM uses reference equality (`==` checks object identity, not contents!), breaking `case class` structural `equals`

questions.prompt: What does `Nothing` as a return type or type argument (e.g., `Nil: List[Nothing]`) allow?

options.text: Because `Nothing` is a subtype of every type, `List[Nothing]` (`Nil`) is a valid `List[T]` for any `T` (via covariance `+A`)

questions.prompt: What does `xs.exists(p)` vs `xs.forall(p)` check?

options.text: `exists` returns `true` if at least one element satisfies `p`; `forall` returns `true` if *every* element satisfies `p` (vacuously `true` on empty)

questions.prompt: What does `unapply` in a companion object enable?

options.text: Avoids runtime object allocation in many single-field wrapper cases (except when boxed in generics/arrays)

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `Option` / `Either` interop in Scala. (Select all that apply.)
Why should you write `Option(javaVal)` instead of `Some(javaVal)` when wrapping a nullable Java return value?

options.text: `Some(null)` creates a `Some` containing `null` (which still causes NPE!), whereas `Option(null)` produces `None`
